decisions.statement: The arguments a command takes are handed in as pages rather than spelled here.
An argument no page the command names carries is refused rather than passed over.
The refusal names every argument the command takes.
An argument carrying no value is true where a call says it and false where none does.
A whole number is answered as a number and true or false as true or false.
A whole number past the largest a number holds exactly is refused rather than read.
A whole number is read as the call wrote it, so one padded with spaces is refused.
A repeating argument gathers its values in the order the values are said.
A repeating argument no call said is an empty list.
A default handed in with the narrowing is answered over the one the argument's page states.
An argument that does not repeat is refused where one call says it twice.
A value that will not narrow is refused for the value alone rather than as one nothing said.
A value is read whole, so the spaces around it are the value's own.
An argument handed an empty value is refused however it was spelled, and counts as unsaid.
That refusal names the empty value the way the call wrote it.
An argument whose value is another argument is an argument no value follows.
Whether a command needs an argument is handed in rather than read off the argument.
Every refusal a call earns is gathered rather than the first alone.
The key an argument is answered under is that argument's slug written in camel.
Nothing here reads a page or reaches an index.
Nothing here prints.
A word that is no flag fills the arguments taken as words, in the order named.
An argument is taken at its flag only where the command takes it at a flag.
A refusal names an argument the command takes as a word alone by its placeholder.
A refusal names an argument the way the call reached it, and both ways where none did.
A word spelled as a flag is refused rather than filling an argument.
An argument said as a word and at its flag in one call is refused.
Two arguments one call may not say together are refused where a call says both.
A pair both entries state is refused once.
A group one call must say one of is refused where a call says none of them.
Arguments naming each other that way are one group rather than pairs.
That refusal names every argument in the group and is said once.
A group is counted by the spellings its refusal names rather than by its members.
A value that will not narrow still answers for the group it is in.
A flag the command takes no argument at is refused rather than filling the argument before it.
A word opening with one dash the command takes no argument at is a value.
A bare dash is the value naming what is piped in rather than a flag.
How many times a call may say an argument is handed in rather than read off the argument.
A repeating word argument takes every word from its own place on.
More words than a command takes are refused saying how many either side is and naming the spare.
Every word after a bare `--` fills a word argument rather than being read as a flag.
An argument is known to be needed here, and what that argument must be one of is not.
A set read at run time is weighed by adding to this refusal rather than by reading the call.
An argument said `--flag=value` carries what follows the first equals.
A value opening with two dashes is handed to a flag written with an equals.
An argument carrying no value is refused where a call writes an equals after it.
A word said after a bare `--` keeps an equals in it rather than being parted at one.

definition: a call's words read against the narrowings handed in
